entities.name: Methyl indole carboxylate
observations: The input structure is a methyl aryl ester on a chloro-substituted indole-like fused heteroaromatic core.
The methyl ester is converted to the corresponding carboxylic acid in the product.

entities.name: Methyl ester hydrolysis
observations: Net transformation is methyl ester cleavage to a carboxylic acid, with methanol lost after aqueous workup.
No exact empirical ORD record was found for this specific substrate; proposed conditions are textbook/plausible.

entities.name: Aqueous base saponification
observations: Plausible reagents include LiOH, NaOH, or KOH in water/MeOH, THF/H2O, or EtOH/H2O, followed by acidification with HCl or citric acid.
LiOH or NaOH under mild-to-moderate heating is a conventional first choice for this indole-containing methyl ester.

entities.name: Acidic ester hydrolysis
observations: Alternative conditions include aqueous HCl or H2SO4 in MeOH/H2O or AcOH/H2O, with heating as needed.
